body_markdown:
Year-end payroll close-out checklist for 2026
Closing out payroll for 2026 comes down to five procedures. Assign every payment to the year it was paid, check each name and Social Security number against the card, reconcile the four quarterly Forms 941 to the W-2 and W-3 totals, settle December deposits and federal unemployment tax, and load only the 2027 figures already published.
How to lock the wage year by pay date
W-2 entries must be based on wages paid during the calendar year, so the pay date controls, and the IRS instructions give an example in which December 2026 work paid on January 1, 2027 goes on the 2027 form.


What you need first. Every 2026 payment with its pay date, the imputed income list, employees’ tip reports, and any third-party sick pay notices.


1. Sort every payment by the date it was actually or constructively paid. Under 26 CFR 31.3121(a)-2, constructive payment means the wages are credited to the employee’s account or set apart so the employee can draw them at any time, without any substantial limitation or restriction on when or how they are paid.
2. Add imputed income. Taxable fringe benefits, including personal use of an employer vehicle, go in box 1, and in boxes 3 and 5 when they are FICA wages. Group-term life insurance above $50,000 of coverage is wages in boxes 1, 3 and 5, and the amount is also shown in box 12 with code C. The cost is priced with Table 2-2 in Publication 15-B and reduced by what the employee paid. Cash taken instead of a cafeteria plan benefit is box 1 wages. S corporation 2% shareholder health premiums are box 1 wages, and box 3 wages only if not excludable under section 3121(a)(2)(B).
3. Decide on the special accounting rule. Taxable noncash fringe benefits provided in the last two months of the year can be treated as paid in the next year under this optional rule. Affected employees must use the same period, and the employer must notify them of it. The rule does not cover a transfer of real property or of personal property of a kind normally held for investment.
4. Collect cash tip reports. Employees report cash tips by the 10th of the month after the month received, and no report is required for a month with tips of less than $20. Tips are considered paid when the employee reports them, so a December report received in January belongs to 2027.
5. Ask each third party that paid sick pay for its notice. If it tells the employer in time, the employer may be required to report the sick pay on the W-2s, and if not, the third party prepares them.
6. Fix withholding before the year closes. Under-withheld income tax and Additional Medicare Tax are recovered on or before the last day of the calendar year, excess income tax or Additional Medicare Tax withheld is repaid in the same year, and a Form 941-X income tax adjustment covers only errors found in the year the wages were paid, apart from an administrative error or a section 3509 case.


Hypothetical example. An employee has $200,000 of group-term life coverage, and the Table 2-2 rate for the employee’s age is $0.15 per $1,000 per month. Coverage above $50,000 is $150,000, or 150 thousands, so 150 x $0.15 x 12 = $270.00. The employee paid $100, so $170.00 goes in boxes 1, 3 and 5.


What a correct result looks like. Each 2026 payment sits in the year it was paid, every taxable benefit and tip report is recorded with its pay date, and withholding fixes are finished before year end.
How to check names, Social Security numbers and addresses
What you need first. The payroll register, the Social Security cards on file, and access to the Social Security Number Verification Service.


1. Enter each employee’s name and Social Security number exactly as the card shows them, and write the address with the number, street, and apartment or suite number. A W-2 with a wrong name or number can draw a penalty unless there is reasonable cause.
2. Run the name and number of each employee paid in 2026 through the Social Security Administration’s Social Security Number Verification Service, which checks employee names and numbers for wage reporting. It takes up to 10 names per screen with instant results or a file of up to 250,000 overnight. Use is limited to current or former employees and to W-2 purposes.
3. After a name change, keep the name on the original card until the employee shows the corrected card, and then file a Form W-2c for the most recent W-2 only, because it is not necessary to correct prior years when the previous name and number were used for those years.
4. Collect a Form W-9 from each contractor likely to meet the Form 1099-NEC test, which includes payments for services in the course of business of at least $2,000 during the year to someone who is not an employee. The IRS suggests requesting the W-9, and backup withholding may apply when no taxpayer identification number is on file.


What a correct result looks like. Every name and number on the register matches the card, and each contractor who may receive a Form 1099-NEC has a taxpayer identification number on file.
How to reconcile the quarterly returns to the year-end wage totals
The IRS matches the four quarterly Forms 941 to the W-3 totals. Using a payroll provider does not relieve an employer of the responsibility to ensure that Forms W-2 are furnished to employees and that Forms W-2 and W-3 are filed with the SSA correctly and on time.


What you need first. The four 2026 Forms 941 with any Forms 941-X, the year-end W-2 box totals, and the year’s plan and benefit reports.


1. Compare the year-end totals in boxes 2, 3, 5 and 7 on the W-2s and W-3 with the four Forms 941. For 2026 wages, the W-2 and W-3 are due February 1, 2027 (January 31 is a Sunday).
2. Compare the tax boxes. The Form 941 tax lines run approximately twice W-3 boxes 4 and 6, except for Additional Medicare Tax. That tax is withheld from the pay period in which an employee’s wages pass $200,000 through the end of the calendar year, and when it is withheld, the Form 941 Medicare amount will not be twice the Medicare tax withheld shown in W-3 box 6.
3. Run the box checks. Confirm each employee’s Social Security wages are at or below the 2026 base of $184,500, that box 5 is not less than the sum of boxes 3 and 7 (the SSA rejects those W-2s), and that the payer name and EIN are the same on the W-2, the W-3 and the Forms 941.
4. Check plan reporting. Elective deferrals other than Roth deferrals stay out of box 1 but are reported in box 3, and Roth deferrals go in boxes 1, 3 and 5 with code AA, BB or EE in box 12. Employer HSA contributions, including those made through a cafeteria plan, use code W. Dependent care benefits go in box 10.
5. Note the 2026 reporting items. A W-2 is required for wages of $2,000 or more even when no tax was withheld. Qualified overtime compensation uses the new code TT, cash tips the new code TP, and the Treasury Tipped Occupation Code the new box 14b. An employer’s voluntary payment of an employee’s state paid family and medical leave contribution is W-2 wages. Which plans apply varies by state, so ask the state, city or local tax department.


Hypothetical example. Forms 941 reporting Social Security wages of $250,000, $255,000, $260,000 and $265,000, with every employee below the wage base, total $1,030,000. At 12.4% the Forms 941 show $127,720.00 of Social Security tax, and at 6.2% W-3 box 4 shows $63,860.00, exactly twice. In a separate case, one employee is paid $288,000, so Additional Medicare Tax is ($288,000 minus $200,000) x 0.9% = $792.00. W-3 box 6 shows $4,176.00 of Medicare tax (1.45%) plus $792.00, or $4,968.00. The Forms 941 show $8,352.00 (2.9%) plus $792.00, or $9,144.00, which is not twice $4,968.00 because of the $792.00.


What a correct result looks like. Every difference between the Forms 941 and the W-2 and W-3 totals has an explanation in a reconciliation kept with the payroll records, and the box checks pass.
How to close out fourth-quarter deposits and unemployment tax
What you need first. The December 2026 payroll tax liability, FUTA liability by quarter with any amount carried forward, and state unemployment tax statements.


1. Schedule the December deposit. Monthly depositors deposit payments made during a month by the 15th day of the following month, which puts the deposit for December 2026 payments on Friday, January 15, 2027, unless the $100,000 next-day deposit rule applies.
2. Mark the fourth-quarter Form 941 date. It is due by the last day of the month after the quarter ends, or the next business day when that day is a Saturday, Sunday, or legal holiday. January 31, 2027 is a Sunday, so for 2026 wages the due date is Monday, February 1, 2027, or Wednesday, February 10, 2027 when timely deposits paid the quarter’s taxes in full.
3. Apply the FUTA test. Quarterly FUTA liability of $500 or less carries forward, and a liability over $500 triggers a deposit. In the fourth quarter, if the liability plus any earlier undeposited amounts is over $500, the entire amount is deposited by the due date of Form 940, and if it is $500 or less it can be deposited or paid with the return. The draft 2026 Instructions for Form 940 give February 1, 2027 as that due date, or February 10, 2027 when all FUTA was deposited on time.
4. Check the credit. The full FUTA credit needs state unemployment tax paid in full by the due date of Form 940. In a credit reduction state, the extra tax is considered incurred in the fourth quarter. The Department of Labor announces any credit reduction states after November 10 each year, so as of October 2026 the 2026 list is not final.
5. Confirm state unemployment tax. It varies by state, and the Department of Labor lists state unemployment tax contacts by state.
6. Add Affordable Care Act reporting if it applies. Employers with 50 or more full-time employees, including full-time equivalents, in the previous year also file Forms 1094-C and 1095-C. The draft 2026 instructions for those forms give March 2, 2027 for furnishing statements and March 1, 2027 for paper filing or March 31, 2027 for electronic filing.


Hypothetical example. Assume the full credit applies with no credit reduction, so FUTA is 0.6% of wages. Quarterly FUTA wages of $60,000, $20,000, $0 and $10,000 produce liabilities of $360.00, $120.00, $0.00 and $60.00. The running totals through the third quarter are $360, $480 and $480, each $500 or less, so each carries forward. The fourth quarter brings the total to $540, which is over $500, so the employer deposits $540 by the due date of Form 940.


What a correct result looks like. The December deposit is scheduled, FUTA is deposited or carried forward under the $500 rule, and state unemployment tax is paid by the due date of Form 940.
How to load next year’s published figures and set up January
What you need first. The list of published 2027 figures and a roster of employees whose Forms W-4 claim exemption from withholding.


1. Load the Social Security base. For earnings in 2027 the Social Security base is $192,300, and Medicare has no wage limit.
2. Load the HSA limits. The 2027 HSA limits are $4,500 self-only and $9,000 family.
3. Hold the other 2027 federal figures. As of October 2026 the IRS has not published 2027 amounts for 401(k) deferrals, catch-up contributions, the Roth catch-up wage threshold, health FSAs, transportation benefits, withholding tables or the inflation-adjusted reporting threshold. Flag each one to revisit once published.
4. Test 2026 catch-up contributions against the Roth threshold. The Roth catch-up wage threshold is $150,000, measured on 2025 wages, and it decides whether an employee’s 2026 catch-up contributions must be made as Roth contributions. The requirement applies when the employee’s prior-year wages with the plan sponsor, as defined in section 3121(a), exceeded that amount and the plan has Roth features that offer catch-up contributions. The requirement does not apply to SEP or SIMPLE plans. The final regulation, 26 CFR 1.414(v)-2, applies to contributions in taxable years beginning after December 31, 2026, and a reasonable, good faith interpretation standard applies before then.
5. Follow up on exempt Forms W-4. An exemption from income tax withholding lasts one calendar year. An employee who claims exemption must submit a new Form W-4 by February 16, 2027. Without a new form the employer withholds as Single, and a late form is not retroactive, so the employer does not refund tax withheld while the exempt status was not in place.
6. Set retention. Employers must keep employment tax records for at least 4 years, including copies of Forms W-4. Keep W-2 and W-3 copies, including undeliverable W-2s, for at least 4 years. Keep copies of Forms 1099-NEC for at least 3 years from the due date, or 4 years if backup withholding was imposed.


What a correct result looks like. Only published 2027 figures are loaded, each unpublished figure is flagged to revisit, and every exempt employee has a new Form W-4 request on the calendar.
Frequently asked questions
Which year’s W-2 covers wages paid on January 1, 2027 for a December 2026 pay period?
The 2027 W-2 covers them, because the form reports wages by the date they are paid.
What if an employee’s name or Social Security number does not match Social Security records?
Check the employee’s name and number with the Social Security Number Verification Service, then enter them as the card shows them. After a name change, the original card’s name stays on the form until the employee shows the corrected card.
Which 2027 figures can employers load now?
As of October 2026, employers can load the Social Security wage base of $192,300 and the HSA limits of $4,500 self-only and $9,000 family. The IRS has not published the 401(k), catch-up, Roth threshold, health FSA or withholding-table amounts for 2027.
When is fourth-quarter FUTA deposited?
The fourth-quarter FUTA liability plus any earlier undeposited amounts is deposited in full by the Form 940 due date when the total is over $500, and a total of $500 or less may be deposited or paid with the return.
Does a November fringe benefit belong on the 2026 or 2027 W-2?
A taxable noncash fringe benefit provided in November can be treated as paid in 2027 when the employer uses the optional special accounting rule for the last two months of the year.
